objective: Make one versioned rule set decide what may leave the process, apply it where untrusted text becomes an artifact, and prove with tests that an injected credential never reaches a structured log line, an evaluation report, a runner diagnostic or a model-call record.
decision_supported: Can an operator answer, from the artifact alone, whether it was scrubbed and by which rules, while run_id, sequence_no and evidence references still join it to its run?
acceptance: redaction rules are centralized in one module and identified by a version string
known secret formats are scrubbed: GitHub tokens, GitHub fine-grained tokens, sk- model keys, Slack tokens, AWS key IDs, JWTs and PEM private-key blocks
Authorization, Cookie, Bearer, URL userinfo, credential query parameters, credential CLI flags and credential environment assignments are scrubbed
arbitrary credential-named keys are scrubbed, including keys inside a nested credential object
nested payloads, exception text, runner command lines and failing-runner stderr are covered
redacted output stays valid JSON, keeps its record shape, and preserves run_id, sequence_no, timestamp, event_id, action_id and evidence_refs
a scrubbed record names the rule version that produced it, and an unscrubbed record carries no marker
raw evidence such as frames, recordings and prompts is replaced by a reference marker while evidence_refs, camera_id and content hashes survive
tests fail when a secret is present in a log line, a report or a runner diagnostic after an injected failure
the published summary is scrubbed as a copy, so the in-memory summary is never mutated
the hardening handbook documents the rule set, the preserved fields, the evidence-by-reference rule and the limits of redaction
evidence: Task Packet schema validation output with exit code
targeted pytest output listing the collected Issue #92 test names, pass counts and exit codes
mutation probe 1 output: with redact_mapping and redact_value reduced to a pass-through, 6 tests fail, so the suite detects a missing redactor
mutation probe 2 output: with the free-text token rules disabled, 22 tests fail, so the suite detects a missing format rule
injected-failure output showing a failing runner that writes a GitHub token to stderr raises a scrubbed RuntimeError, and the published summary contains neither the token nor the model key
an end-to-end structured-log record showing a scrubbed message and details with the redaction rule version while run_id and sequence_no are unchanged
make test, make contract, make scenario-check, make golden-check, make context-check and make docs output with exit codes
final git diff --check and git diff --name-only output proving every changed path is allowed
stop_conditions: A credential appears in the output of any command in this packet.
Stopping the leak requires changing interfaces/, libs/contracts/, robot/control/ or firmware/.
A redaction rule cannot preserve run_id, sequence_no or evidence_refs, so scrubbing would break correlation.
The only way to pass the tests is to assert against a substring instead of the bytes an artifact would contain.
Redaction is reimplemented in a second module instead of extending workbench.application.redaction.
data_classification: internal; every credential used in the tests is synthetic and format-only, with no live or valid secret committed
model_policy: no model call is needed; the rules are deterministic regular expressions and name classifiers
risks_and_fallbacks: A false positive would scrub an honest value. Identifier fields are copied through, metadata suffixes win over raw-evidence names, and token-count names are excluded, so counts, hashes and references keep their value.
A new artifact producer could bypass the logger. The rule set lives in one importable module so a new consumer adds an import rather than a second implementation.
A secret with no known format and no credential-shaped name cannot be found in free text; this is documented as a limit rather than claimed as coverage.
Raw media is replaced by a marker. The referenced store is operator-owned and access-controlled outside this repository, so the test can only assert that content never enters the artifact.
